title: Scawton (near Helmsley) Force) Memorial
memorial_type: Plaque (originally on tree at crash site, relocated to Scawton Church porch after tree fell); display of wreaths and crosses
narrative: Returning from their 38th operational mission over Germany, the Free French crew of Halifax NR287 arrived to find Elvington airfield congested and were unable to land. Cdt Ostre flew the aircraft north to wait, but with damaged instruments and zero visibility the Halifax struck a stone wall near Scawton, North Yorkshire. Five of the nine airmen aboard were killed, including navigator Lt Leplus; two survived. The crew flew with 347 Squadron and included Marcel Vigouroux, Yves Even, Louis Baillon, and Henri Granier — airmen who had completed thirty-seven previous missions before this fatal return flight.
memorial_details: | Feature | Detail | |---------|--------| | **Village Memorial** | Inverse shield-shaped slate memorial with French inscription in gold and three French aviation badges; unveiled September 1957 in Elvington village | | **Yorkshire Air Museum** | Allied Air Forces Memorial on the former airfield; restored Halifax bomber (one of only three in the world); memorial to women who served in WWII | | **York Minster** | French Air Force memorial plaque supported by RAF | | **Condition** | Excellent (museum site professionally maintained) | | **Access** | Yorkshire Air Museum, Halifax Way, Elvington, York YO41 4AU; open to public |
cause_of_loss: Unable to land due to airfield congestion; flew north to wait; damaged instruments and zero visibility; struck stone wall

maintainer.notes: Plaque relocated to Scawton Church porch after tree at crash site fell.

external_narratives.summary: Detailed crew page for 347 Squadron Halifax III NR287 L8-C piloted by Cdt George Ostre. The aircraft crashed at Scawton on 16 March 1945 while returning from a raid on Hagen, with 5 killed and 2 admitted to Northallerton Hospital.
key_details: Crew buried at Harrogate (Stonefall) then returned to France

external_narratives.summary: Yorkshire Air Museum page documenting the Free French squadrons at Elvington during WWII. 346 'Guyenne' and 347 'Tunisie' were the only French heavy bomber squadrons in the UK, formed from June 1944 and operating until October 1945.
key_details: 346 and 347 Squadrons were only Free French heavy bomber units in UK
Nearly half of squadron members killed
Yorkshire Air Museum is now on the former airfield

external_narratives.summary: York Stories page documenting WW2 bomber crash sites in Yorkshire, including the Scawton Halifax crash. Five Free French airmen died when their damaged Halifax flew into high ground west of Helmsley in zero visibility after being unable to land due to airfield congestion.
key_details: Aircraft flew into high ground 5 miles west of Helmsley

external_narratives.summary: Detailed research page on 347 'Tunisie' Squadron at Elvington. Halifax NR287 was built by E.E.C. Ltd at Salmesbury and delivered to 347 Squadron on 2 December 1944, only three months before it was lost at Scawton.
key_details: NR287 built by E.E.C. Ltd at Salmesbury
Lost after only 3 months with the squadron
